description: Display-engine timing generator: one pixel clock of the raster is retired per accepted beat, so a line of H_TOTAL clocks takes exactly H_TOTAL beats and a frame takes H_TOTAL*V_TOTAL beats, all counted in fabric. A program beat is c[31]=1 with the totals in a and b and c[30:0]=0: a[9:0]=H_ACTIVE, a[16:10]=H front porch, a[24:17]=H sync width, a[30:25]=H back porch, b[10:0]=V_ACTIVE, b[18:11]=V front porch, b[22:19]=V sync width (lines), b[30:23]=V back porch, b[31]=0; the totals are built with three adds each (no multiply) and the beat plots clock (0,0) of the new frame, clearing the frame counter. A step beat carries the feeder budgets a[9:0]=clocks per line available, b[9:0]=lines per frame available (0 = unbounded), with a[31:10]=b[31:10]=c=0. Fault (result=aux=0, state kept): a reserved field is nonzero, a zero active area or zero sync width was programmed, a total exceeds the 1024-clock raster counter, or a step arrives before the generator was programmed. State: 9:0 x, 19:10 y, 31:20 H_TOTAL, 43:32 V_TOTAL, 53:44 H_ACTIVE, 65:54 hsync start, 77:66 back-porch start, 87:78 V_ACTIVE, 99:88 vsync start, 111:100 V back-porch start, 119:112 completed frames, 120 programmed. result[9:0]=x, [19:10]=y, [20]=data-enable (inside both active windows), [21]=inside the hsync pulse, [22]=inside the vsync pulse, [23]=inside the vertical active window, [25:24]=horizontal phase (0 active, 1 front porch, 2 sync, 3 back porch), [26]=line start, [27]=line end, [28]=frame start, [29]=frame complete, [30]=this beat programmed the generator, [31]=H_TOTAL exceeds the line budget just presented. aux[9:0]=H_TOTAL, [19:10]=V_TOTAL, [20]=vsync rising strobe, [21]=hsync rising strobe, [22]=last active clock of an active line, [23]= V_TOTAL exceeds the frame budget just presented, [31:24]=frames completed.
hardware_advantage: A timing generator in firmware is a decrementing counter plus three compares and a branch per pixel clock, and its output skew depends on interrupt latency; this core issues de, hsync, vsync, the phase code and the coordinates for one pixel clock every enabled beat at II=1 from one unbroken counter cone, so every line and frame edge is exact and the budget flags prove the feeder can keep up before the first pixel moves.
provenance: original source authored in this workspace; no third-party RTL imported
qualification: engineering candidate; not certified production or side-channel protection
